# Sources

Read 2026-10-29. "Full" means the page itself was read; "summary" means only a search summary, an excerpt, or a
secondary write-up was read; "blocked" means the page refused the fetch (403) and only its title, abstract or
search snippet was seen. Vendor means the publisher sells the thing it measures or teaches.

## SPIN (Rackham)

| Source | URL | Read | One line |
|---|---|---|---|
| Huthwaite, Neil Rackham on the research behind SPIN | https://www.huthwaiteinternational.com/blog/neil-rackham-research-spin | Full | Interview transcript: coaching method, 0.85 observer correlation, one project of 60 salespeople and 360 calls, client firms Xerox, IBM, Motorola. The 35,000 calls and the 17% lift appear only inside skeptics' questions; Rackham disputes the cause, not the number. Author's own firm. |
| Wikipedia, Neil Rackham | https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neil_Rackham | Full | 30 researchers, 35,000 calls, 20+ countries, 12 years, $1M; says he sought support from Xerox and IBM; gives no salesperson count. |
| Sales Society, The fascinating science of SPIN selling | https://salessociety.substack.com/p/the-fascinating-science-of-spin-selling | Full | Secondary: open vs closed made no difference; closing and objection handling not decisive; "10x need-payoff" with no baseline. |
| Routledge, SPIN Selling book page | https://www.routledge.com/SPIN-Selling-1st-Edition/Rackham/p/book/9780566076893 | Summary | Publisher description of the book. |
| O'Reilly, SPIN Selling table of contents | https://oreilly.com/library/view/spin-selling/9781260027099 | Summary | Chapters on benefits in major sales, preventing objections, evaluating the model (Motorola Canada). |
| claudeskills.info SPIN skill page | https://claudeskills.info/skills/getagentseal/founder-playbook/spin-selling/ | Summary | Third-party: photo-store closing figures 72 to 76% and 42 to 33%. Unverified. |
| SuperSummary, SPIN Selling | https://www.supersummary.com/spin-selling/summary/ | Summary | Advantages lead to objections in large sales; explicit needs and benefits. |

## Challenger

| Source | URL | Read | One line |
|---|---|---|---|
| HBR, The End of Solution Sales (Adamson, Dixon, Toman, 2012) | https://hbr.org/2012/07/the-end-of-solution-sales | Summary (excerpt only, paywall) | Customers can define solutions without reps. |
| Challenger Inc., The Challenger Customer profiles | https://challengerinc.com/the-challenger-customer-profiles/ | Full | Mobilizers, 31% more likely high performer, 700 stakeholders, 135 attributes, factor analysis. Vendor. |
| Inks, Avila, Talbert 2019, J. of Global Scholars of Marketing Science 29(1) | https://ideas.repec.org/a/taf/jgsmks/v29y2019i1p88-98.html | Abstract | Relationship selling vs Challenger; reviews the criticisms. Peer reviewed. |
| Rapp et al. 2014, JPSSM 34(4), "Salespeople as knowledge brokers: a review and critique of the Challenger sales model" | https://research.ohio.edu/rapp-adam/research-0 | Summary (listing only) | Peer-reviewed critique; authorship from Adam Rapp's publication list; text not read. |
| Capon, Revisiting The Challenger Sale (Columbia) | https://business.columbia.edu/faculty/research/revisiting-challenger-sale-breakthrough-built-flimsy-foundation | Blocked | Title: "breakthrough built on a flimsy foundation". |
| CustomerThink, After 10,000 hours of challenging customers | https://customerthink.com/after-10000-hours-of-challenging-customers-are-your-sales-reps-experts/ | Summary | Practitioner critique; 2,000 high performers in the original sample. |
| Impact Plus, the 5 types of sellers | https://www.impactplus.com/blog/the-5-types-of-sellers-of-the-challenger-sale | Summary | 40% Challengers, 7% Relationship Builders among high performers. Secondary. |

## Practitioners of outreach

| Source | URL | Read | One line |
|---|---|---|---|
| Josh Braun, Ditch the pitch, poke the bear | https://joshbraun.com/ditch-the-pitch-poke-the-bear/ | Full | Neutral vs leading questions, examples. |
| Josh Braun, Cold email CTAs | https://joshbraun.com/cold-email-ctas/ | Full | Time asks bad; status-quo questions good. |
| ContentGrip, Sam McKenna's cold email method | https://www.contentgrip.com/cold-email-method-sam-mckenna/ | Full | Subject only they understand, problem, objection, availability ask; 43% open, 20% reply self-reported. |
| 30MPC podcast 596 with Sam McKenna (transcript) | https://podcastrex.com/shows/30-minutes-to-presidents-club-no-nonsense-sales/596-this-cold-email-formula-gets-20-replies-exact-templates/transcript | Blocked (summary) | "Would it make sense to anyone else" test. |
| 30MPC newsletter, the data-backed cold email formula | https://www.30mpc.com/newsletter/the-data-backed-cold-email-formula-the-exact-words-length | Full | 85M emails: pitching up to -57%, problem-first +20%, social proof +41%, offer +28%, REPLY Method taught to 10,000 reps. |
| GTMnow, Jason Bay 3-part framework | https://thegtmnewsletter.substack.com/p/your-new-3-part-framework-for-cold-ea3 | Full | "Identify, engage, create", not explained. |
| Bowery Capital, Outbound 3.0 (Jason Bay) | https://bowerycap.com/blog/podcasts/outbound-3-0/ | Summary | REPLY method as a 5-step process. |
| futureproofselling show notes (Jason Bay) | https://futureproofselling.libsyn.com/website/getting-responses-to-emails-and-calls-with-prospecting-expert-jason-bay | Summary | REPLY expanded as Results, Empathy, Personalization, Laser-focus, You. Unconfirmed. |
| Gong, best and worst cold call openers (300M calls) | https://www.gong.io/blog/the-best-and-worst-cold-call-openers-backed-by-data-from-300m-calls | Full | Four opener rates; no sample per opener, no success definition. Vendor. |
| Antoine Buteau, lessons from Farrokh and Cegelski | https://www.antoinebuteau.com/lessons-armand-farrokh-and-nick-cegelski/ | Full | Earn the next 60 s, permission opener, problem / solution / interest email, voicemail+email 5.87% vs 2.73%. Secondary. |
| Stretch VP, cold email outreach | https://stretchvp.substack.com/p/cold-email-outreach | Summary | Allred's "above the line": observation, problem, credibility, solution, call for conversation. Secondary. |
| Lavender, email writing ideas | https://lavender.ai/blog/email-writing-ideas | Summary | Observation, insight, credibility, solution, interest CTA. Vendor. |
| Antoine Buteau, lessons from Becc Holland | https://www.antoinebuteau.com/lessons-from-becc-holland/ | Summary (read in full in `../linkedin-messages/`) | Premise reused across touches; never fake one. |

| Source | URL | Read | One line |
|---|---|---|---|
| Craig Elias, trigger event selling statistics (slides) | https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/trigger-event-selling-statistics/43585662 | Summary | 74% slide attributed to Forrester 2012, measure not stated. |
| CustomerThink, Seeing through the window of discontent (Elias) | https://customerthink.com/seeing_through_window_discontent/ | Summary | Definition of the window. |
| HubSpot, How to overcome the number one objection (Elias) | https://blog.hubspot.com/sales/how-to-overcome-the-number-one-sales-objection | Summary | "10 times more likely to buy", first in. Author's claim. |
| UserGems, signal-based outbound | https://www.usergems.com/the-ai-for-outbound-aeo-hub/signal-based-outbound-what-it-is-and-why-it-beats-volume-first-ai-sdr | Summary | 6 to 20% reply vs 1 to 2%. Vendor. |
| Vantaige, signal-based outbound playbook | https://vantaige.io/blog/signal-based-outbound-playbook-2026 | Summary | 18% vs 3.4%, citing another vendor. Third hand. |
| LinkedIn, How top reps outperform their peers (14 Jan 2015) | https://www.linkedin.com/business/sales/blog/b2b-sales/how-top-reps-outperform-their-peers- | Full | SSI leaders 45% more opportunities, 51% more likely to hit quota; no method. Vendor. |
| Breakcold, social selling statistics | https://breakcold.com/blog/social-selling-statistics | Summary | Repeats the 78% figure without a primary link. |
| Expandi, State of LinkedIn Outreach H2 2026 | https://expandi.io/state-of-linkedin-outreach-h2-2026/ | Full | 13.2M invitations (May 2025 to April 2026); sequence length 1 to 5+ (message 1 is the note in connector campaigns); tie openers ("joining my group" is the sender's group, not a shared one); 22% warm-up figure quoted from its H1 report; no spacing data. Vendor, observational. |
| Expandi, LinkedIn outreach benchmarks 2026 | https://expandi.io/blog/linkedin-outreach-benchmarks-2026/ | Summary | 28.5% acceptance, message reply 10 to 11%, existing connections 16.86%. Vendor. |
| getfuzzy, LinkedIn outreach statistics | https://getfuzzy.ai/blog/linkedin-outreach-statistics | Summary | Profile view +21%, like +39%, no method. Vendor. |
| Gracker, increase LinkedIn acceptance rate | https://gracker.ai/blog/increase-linkedin-acceptance-rate | Summary | "Triple acceptance" warm-up, no method. Vendor. |
| Smartlead, multi-channel outreach | https://smartlead.ai/blog/multi-channel-outreach | Full | Multi-channel "2 to 4x"; the meeting-rate table quoted elsewhere is not on this page. Vendor. |
| Prospeo, multi-channel outreach | https://prospeo.io/s/multi-channel-outreach | Summary | 10 to 14 touches, 3 to 4 days apart. Vendor. |
| Zeliq, sales sequence | https://www.zeliq.com/blog/sales-sequence | Summary | 8 touches over 18 days. Vendor. |
| Causo, H1 2026 multichannel report | https://hub.causo.ai/guides/h1-2026-multichannel-outreach-report | Summary | 5 to 7 touches, citing another vendor. |
| Gong, how to write a sales email (follow-up data) | https://www.gong.io/blog/how-to-write-a-sales-email | Full (re-checked) | 304,174 emails: interest CTA "2x+ more likely to book a meeting" than a time ask. Does NOT contain the guilt follow-up -14% or "fall with each touch"; those are untraced. Vendor. |
